the tube map of yor mind the map is not the territory i went to an illuminating talk by advertising guru and behavioural science expert rory sutherland today one highlight amongst many was his use of the london tube map to illustrate the mental maps we all create in our minds as means for navigating and understanding the world just like the london tube map our mental maps contain distortions all based on the way we laid down and encoded them experience after experience and from a psychology perspective these distortions are manifest as cognitive biases and heuristics now rory was highlighting how problems can arise when we are all begin to use the same maps what i took from this was how societal influences norms and pressures all accumulate to create that conditioned part of our minds manifest as part of our cultural identity values belief customs and even preferences that is a big rabbit hole to chase ourselves down and as i see it if we are on that journey the more self aware we become over time the grip on our individual values and beliefs usually loosens as we see through the enormous power that societal and tribal conditioning has on the way to think and feel and perceive the world for some people this is challenging to realise for others it is truly liberating our maps are not fixed as part of my teaching and coaching the deepest area of exploration is not the content of our unique map of the world but how we create those maps and what keeps us so often beholden by these maps which can become entrenched and inflexible particularly when we believe that our map is reality i ask clients to reflect on what the maps are made of and to explore that if the maps are not fixed and are only held in place via our beliefs albeit unconsciously most of the time not only can these maps change but they do not have to control us waking up to how we create our own realities can be transformational albeit it is a journey that can challenge our assumptions and beliefs to their core and it has no absolute end if that is the price of greater freedom from the map i am willing to keep paying my subs

sometimes if we are anxious it can be tempting to bury our head in the sand and hope the thing we are worried about will just go away this is not a helpful strategy as it means that not only does the problem remain unsolved but we now have a second problem of being anxious about the first problem this can manifest in overt ways such as worrying rumination and insomnia and it can also manifest in the body through digestive problems headaches and migraines back pain and tooth clenching and grinding when an anxiety provoking issue arises a good first step to dealing with it is to ask yourself if you can take practical steps to solve or mitigate the problem if yes get on and do so quickly avoiding the temptation to procrastinate may be uncomfortable in the moment and require courage but will save you a lot of worry in the future sometimes the task may be large in which case breaking it down into more manageable chunks can help sometimes all we can do is take baby steps towards a resolution but keep on moving towards the end goal if the problem is not one you can solve then you will need to manage your emotional response to the ongoing situation the first step to doing this is acceptance which i will be explaining more about in future posts

visitors on a journey moving between a tangible reality and a digital existence through the artist s varied and vibrant works preparatory documents and sketches the display guides viewers through his creative thought process bringing together elements that inform his continued investigation and questioning of how the increasing digitalisation of the world intertwines and dwells within contemporary identities patching elements of the past the present and the preempted future james multimedia works in look what the cat dragged in reflectively tell a story about time teeming with recycled and timeworn fabrics each holding their own tales of former eras and wearers the artist s works manifest characters and scenarios triggered from his childhood memories projecting facets of past encounters into present existence acting as a diary for the audience he showcases works on paper documenting his experiences or thoughts which are later combined and expanded to create the wider narrative of his finished canvases james seeks to reveal the impactful subtleties that exist in everyday interactions and the ever present role digitalisation plays in defining personal identity today through his dreamlike scenarios that blur the lines between fantasy and truth situating viewers within realms known and unknown james unsettling works gesture a visionary commentary on our relationship with the quick mama make up lockdown skin tips after posting my corona hair video yesterday i received quite a few dm s requesting external wellness tips for your skin so i thought its only right that i oblige with the following us home schooling mamas are not got no time for contouring or to cake on foundation for that matter we got kids to feed lessons to teach hence i have found all you really need is a good brush and a bronzer for your cheek bones i personally use mineralise skinfinish natural in dark by mac honestly this has been my go to mama on the move essentials for years just a quick brush on to my cheek bones a dab to any oily arrears and it just wakes your skins natural warm glow up giving you that honey due look eyes our eyes are the window to our soul for a busy mama like me i only use things in my mama make up tool kit if like me you want results but you are not got time for any surgical looking lash metal curlers all the other time consuming jazz which takes way too long you may want to consider mac extended play gigablack mascara mac hr eye concealer a dark eye shadow all three take about second each to apply and i am done seriously in under minutes my time saving mini makeup moves listed above has me looking like a mama that is still shining inside out mamas h o aka water we know that our bodies are water so it just makes sense that if you are a mama on the move you need to keep hydrated if you do not have a water machine at home then ensure you have stocked up on oodles of bottles water refreshes your mood replenishes your energy and vitalise the skin lips keep it subtle but w a pop as a mum of x young souls i have come to find that a part of feeling good internally is also extending that love to my outter self centering thought for the day self care manifest in the total care of your being
